location.character: Brampton's first 'New Urbanism' neighbourhood — designed for walkability and inclusive amenities around GO transit
location.go_station: Mount Pleasant GO Station (Kitchener GO Line) — within neighbourhood; opens in 2005 triggered development
location.highway: Highway 410 just east — 40 min drive to downtown Toronto

history.original_settler: James Hunter, Irish immigrant; Hunter family were prosperous farmers; descendants operated farms until early 1900s
history.development_trigger: Mount Pleasant GO Station opened 2005 — this was the catalyst for Mount Pleasant Village development
history.design_concept: Brampton's first New Urbanism neighbourhood — designed around walkability, community square, all-inclusive amenities

market_data.notes: HoodQ does not have a specific Mount Pleasant page. Northwest Brampton April 2026 median $866K is the closest verified benchmark (Realosophy, 37 sales).
sources: realosophy.com Northwest Brampton April 2026 — median $866K, 37 sales

go_station.name: Mount Pleasant GO Station
go_station.note: The GO station is the reason the neighbourhood exists — Mount Pleasant Village was explicitly designed around GO transit access

transit.local_transit: Brampton Züm rapid transit service with local routes
transit.car: Highway 410 just east — 40 min to downtown Toronto by car

architecture.style: Heritage-style New Urbanism — Tudor, Georgian, Arts and Craft architectural details
architecture.garage_design: Garages located at rear of homes in hidden laneways — improves streetscape
architecture.new_development: The Neighbourhoods of Mount Pleasant — 237 units (townhomes and single-family); under development
architecture.street_character: Heritage-style street signs; community square with public art and skating rink; CP Railway station revitalized in civic square

secondary.name: Jean Augustine Secondary School
secondary.source: Fraser Institute 2025; confirmed serving Mount Pleasant in Peel DSB boundary documents

secondary.name: David Suzuki Secondary School
secondary.note: Situated 3 km east of Mount Pleasant GO Station. Eco-focused school.
secondary.source: Fraser Institute 2025; Mapcarta; Peel DSB boundary documents

elementary.notable: Mount Pleasant Village Public School (elementary): 5.9/10 Fraser Institute 2025 (ranked #1640 of Ontario elementary schools)

schools.note: Both secondary schools rated below Ontario's 6.0 provincial average. Elementary school (5.9/10) is very close to provincial average.

creditview_sandalwood_park.location: North end of neighbourhood, Credit River banks
features: Creditview Activity Hub (2018) — first all-inclusive playground of its kind in Ontario, accessible for children with disabilities

angus_morrison_park.trail: 4km Mount Pleasant Recreational Trail — central park location

features: Reflecting pool transforming to skating rink in winter
Revitalized CP Railway station as civic landmark
Trestle Bridge sculpture by Ron Baird (2011)

parks_and_recreation.community_centre: Mount Pleasant Community Centre — gymnasium, playground; adjacent to outdoor skating rink

shopping: In-village commercial: gourmet shops, salons, spas, barbers, restaurants, fashion boutiques around town square
Fortinos on Worthington Avenue (quality food — short drive)
FreshCo at Sandalwood Parkway & Chinguacousy Road
Apple Factory Farm Market (just west, 40+ year landmark) — old-school dressings, sauces, local produce
restaurants: Biryani Culture — halal Pakistani homestyle food, in heritage-style village building
Pane Fresco (inside Fortinos) — 19 pizza varieties, 13 soups, sushi, vegan options
amenities.library: Mount Pleasant branch library — within neighbourhood
